title: Revenue & Customer Intelligence Business Understanding
summary: Built a reporting layer on GC to track freight revenue, customer concentration, route demand, delivery success, and payment mix.
description: Analyzed GC transaction data to turn bookings, customer activity, route movement, delivery status, and payment terms into a clean business reporting view for management, sales, operations, and BI users.
highlights: Measured total freight revenue of 2,170,895 across 250 consignments and 89 customers.
Identified heavy concentration in TBB and TO PAY bookings, which together account for most revenue.
Top customers and routes dominate the business, while delivery status capture needs validation for SLA reporting.

readme.overview: This project turns GC transaction data into a reliable reporting layer for revenue, customer, route, delivery, and payment analysis. The goal is to help management and analysts understand what drives freight revenue, which customers and routes contribute the most volume, and where payment or delivery risk may exist.
readme.problem: GC contains the core revenue and customer activity records, but it is not arranged for fast and consistent analysis. Business users need a dependable view that explains how freight revenue is generated, how concentrated customer demand is, how routes perform, and how payment terms affect cash collection risk.
readme.approach: Structured the analysis around revenue, customer, route, delivery, and payment dimensions. Calculated KPIs for total revenue, consignments, customers, average freight per consignment, and payment split. Reviewed delivery capture and route concentration to highlight data-quality gaps and operational patterns.
salesTrend: TBB and TO PAY together drive 241 of 250 consignments, showing heavy credit dependence.
BANGALORE -> BHIWANDI and HYDERABAD -> VIJAYAWADA account for the largest booking demand.
Only 3 bookings are marked loaded = 'Y', so delivery capture is not reliable enough for SLA reporting.
readme.bottomLine: Revenue is highly concentrated in a few customers and routes, while delivery tracking and payment mix both need tighter control before the reporting layer is used for executive dashboards.

title: Operations & Profitability Optimization Business Understanding
summary: Analyzed GDM dispatch data to measure transport cost, load utilization, transit time, and route profitability.
description: Structured GDM operational records to understand dispatch cost, fleet usage, movement duration, and route efficiency, then linked GC revenue data where needed to estimate route profitability.
highlights: Calculated total transport cost of 3,858,332 across 250 trips with an average transit time of 4.9036 days.
Reviewed route profitability and found both profitable and loss-making lanes after joining GC and GDM data.
A small truck group handled most trips, and the highest-cost routes need review for cost control.

readme.overview: This project turns GDM dispatch records into an operational reporting layer for transport cost, transit time, truck usage, and load efficiency. The goal is to identify where transport spend is highest, which routes are delayed, and how effectively fleet capacity is being used.
readme.problem: GDM records dispatch costs, movement times, truck usage, and load characteristics, but the data needs to be structured into a usable reporting layer. Operations leaders need to know where transport cost is highest, which routes are delayed, and how effectively fleet capacity is being used.
readme.approach: Analyzed dispatch records across route, truck, weight, hire expense, and transit duration fields. Calculated cost and utilization KPIs, then linked GC revenue data by route mapping to understand directional profitability and identify cost-heavy lanes.
salesTrend: Bangalore-Bhiwandi and Bangalore-Chennai create the highest cost exposure.
Several long-haul routes exceed 20 average transit days and should be reviewed for delay causes.
Directional profitability varies sharply after the GC-GDM join, so route margin should be interpreted by lane direction.
readme.bottomLine: Transport spend is concentrated in a few routes and trucks, so the biggest savings opportunity is tighter lane-level cost control and better fleet balancing.

title: Vendor & Cash Flow Management Business Understanding
summary: Measured vendor spend, outstanding payables, payment timing, and penalties from THP records.
description: Evaluated THP payment records to understand vendor spend concentration, unpaid balances, payment timing, tax deduction behavior, and possible data-quality issues in penalty capture.
highlights: Total vendor spend reached 4,328,166, while outstanding payables stood at 2,044,868.
Vendor 20033 dominates spend concentration and should be prioritized in payment planning.
Zero TDS and penalty values, plus a very long average payment cycle, indicate a likely data-capture gap that should be validated.

readme.overview: This project turns THP payment records into a financial reporting layer for vendor spend, outstanding balances, payment timing, and delay-related controls. The goal is to help finance teams monitor cash flow pressure and understand where spend is concentrated.
readme.problem: THP payment records capture vendor hire amounts, outstanding balances, and payment timing, but the data needs a clean business view to support cash flow monitoring. Finance teams need to know which vendors drive spend, how much remains unpaid, and whether the payment cycle is creating liquidity pressure.
readme.approach: Analyzed vendor identifiers, order dates, payable and balance amounts, hire amount, TDS, and delay penalty values. Measured vendor concentration, outstanding liabilities, payment-cycle timing, and monthly hire amount movement to highlight spend patterns and control gaps.
salesTrend: Vendor 20033 dominates total spend and should be prioritized in payment planning.
Hire amounts spike sharply in 2022-12, 2023-04, and 2024-06, suggesting irregular spending patterns.
Zero TDS and penalty values across vendors indicate either clean settlements or a data capture gap that should be checked.
readme.bottomLine: Vendor spend is concentrated, outstanding payables are high, and payment-cycle data needs validation before it can support tighter cash-flow governance.

title: Northwind Sales Data Warehouse & Analytics
summary: Northwind warehouse results show strong performance with clear concentration: a small set of products, customers, employees, and shipping partners drive most revenue.
description: Analyzed Northwind warehouse outputs to evaluate KPI performance, contributor concentration, and trend behavior. Findings show healthy revenue and order values, but meaningful dependency on top performers across products, accounts, employees, and carriers.
highlights: Total revenue reached 1,265,792.93 with 830 orders and average order value of 1,525.05.
Cote de Blaye, top customers, and key sales employees account for a large share of commercial performance.
Monthly revenue strengthened through 1996, with May 1996 at 129,247.26 and June treated as partial data.

readme.overview: Executive summary: Northwind warehouse analysis shows clear sales concentration patterns. Overall performance is solid, with total revenue above 1.26 million and average order value above 1.5 thousand.
readme.problem: The business needed a reader-friendly executive view of KPI health and concentration risk across products, customers, employees, and shipping. Leadership also needed confidence in trend interpretation where final-month data may be incomplete.
readme.approach: Used the dimensional warehouse outputs to compute KPI snapshot metrics, rank contributors, and assess trend behavior over time. Findings were organized into product, customer, employee, shipping, and monthly growth insights for executive consumption.

items: Account value is more important than order count alone
Performance gap indicates uneven sales distribution
Shipment volume and revenue move closely together

salesTrend: Sales strength increased from early 1994 into much stronger monthly performance in 1996.
Monthly revenue crossed 100,000 in multiple 1996 months, peaking at 129,247.26 in May 1996.
June 1996 should be treated as incomplete month data, not a confirmed decline.
readme.bottomLine: Northwind is performing well, but business contribution is not evenly balanced. A narrow set of top performers drives most revenue, so growth strategy should protect key contributors while reducing concentration risk.
readme.impact: Sales leadership can prioritize top accounts and product categories, operations can maintain strength in core carriers while balancing service coverage, and reporting can standardize trend comparisons using complete-month logic.

title: Netflix Content Analytics & SQL Insights
summary: Cleaned 26,421 raw rows down to 8,807 deduplicated titles and produced KPI-ready EDA from netflix_clean_final.
description: Executed full Netflix SQL workflow from table creation to EDA on netflix_clean_final. Findings cover data quality outcomes, catalog mix, rating distribution, growth slowdown after peak year, country/genre concentration risk, and stakeholder recommendations.
highlights: Deduplication removed 17,614 duplicate rows and finalized 8,807 clean records for analysis.
Movies represent 69.62% of catalog while TV Shows account for 30.38%.
Top-5 country share is 58.34% (medium concentration risk) and top-5 genre share is 17.95% (low risk).

readme.overview: Simple EDA report based on cleaned view netflix_clean_final in netflix_db. All KPI answers are derived from the cleaned analytical layer, not the raw table.
readme.problem: Raw data included missing fields, standardization issues, and heavy duplication, which reduced trust in downstream EDA. Stakeholders needed clean KPI answers for content mix, rating dominance, growth trend, and concentration risk.
readme.approach: Ran SQL scripts in sequence: 01_create_tables.sql, 02_load_data.sql, 03_data_exploration.sql, 04_cleaning_views.sql, and 05_eda_queries.sql. Enabled local_infile for LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE, then validated post-cleaning quality checks and concentration metrics.
salesTrend: Catalog additions grew strongly up to peak year 2019, then slowed in 2020 and 2021.
2021 additions were 1,498 titles, a YoY drop of 381 vs 2020.
Country concentration risk is medium (58.34%) while genre concentration risk is low (17.95%).
readme.bottomLine: The cleaned view delivers reliable catalog intelligence, but this is metadata-only analysis and does not include watch-time, engagement, or revenue behavior.
readme.impact: Recommendations delivered for content strategy, acquisition, marketing, and analytics operations: keep movie strength while scaling selective TV investment, monitor country concentration quarterly, maintain metadata validation checks, and retain outlier monitoring during recurring loads.

title: Electric Vehicle Adoption Analytics Dashboard
summary: EV market analysis shows rapid post-2020 scaling, clear BEV dominance, and strong concentration around Tesla and regional adoption hubs.
description: Built a Power BI dashboard and analytical narrative for EV market composition, growth trajectory, geography, manufacturer concentration, model preference, and CAFV eligibility quality. Insights highlight both momentum and concentration risk.
highlights: Total EV vehicles reached 150,440 with BEV share at 77.62% and PHEV share at 22.38%.
Tesla leads with 68,963 vehicles (~46% of market), far ahead of the next manufacturers.
Growth accelerates strongly after 2020, with 2023 as highest year and 2024 treated as partial.

readme.overview: Executive summary: the EV market is in a strong scaling phase with clear BEV dominance, high manufacturer concentration, and meaningful geographic clustering. Adoption momentum is strongest post-2020.
readme.problem: Stakeholders needed a clear market narrative across composition, growth, geography, make/model leadership, and policy-linked eligibility. Existing reporting did not frame concentration risk and incomplete-year effects well enough for decision-making.
readme.approach: Used Power Query and DAX to build KPI snapshots, growth timelines, market-share rankings, and incentive-eligibility analysis. Structured findings for strategy, operations, and policy interpretation while clearly flagging partial-period and unknown-category limitations.

items: BMW, Kia, Toyota, Volkswagen, Volvo, Jeep follow
Tesla Model S and Model X - strong presence
Chevrolet Bolt EV - popular non-Tesla model
Unknown share indicates metadata or policy-mapping gaps
Adoption is heavily concentrated in Washington State
Seattle-area counties are major EV hubs
Regional penetration is uneven, indicating expansion opportunity

salesTrend: Adoption was gradual through 2018-2019, then accelerated sharply after 2020.
2021-2023 captures the strongest growth phase, with 2023 near 37K vehicles.
2024 appears lower due to partial-year data and should not be treated as structural decline.
readme.bottomLine: The EV market is scaling fast and BEVs are clearly leading, but concentration by manufacturer and geography remains high. This creates both momentum and dependency risk.
readme.impact: Actionable implications include targeting underpenetrated regions, improving incentive eligibility data clarity, sustaining BEV-focused strategy, and monitoring concentration risk while new players and infrastructure scale.
